Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (`eslint.config.js` / `check:lint-rule-coverage`); rationale: class (a) — ⭐ **three controls in one run yielding three distinct states**, which is the cleanest discrimination in today's batch:

```
vitest.config.mts        → isPathIgnored: true, config: undefined   NOT WALKED
playwright.config.ts     → 116 rules                                 walked + ruled
scripts/github-slug.mjs  → 0 rules, but WALKED                       the #7908 class
```

⭐ *"`undefined` is not 'zero rules' — it is ESLint declining to look."* ⇒ That sentence is the whole finding, and it is what makes this a **different** defect from objectui#7908 rather than more of it. `Bug`.

The cause is read off the flat-config rules rather than inferred: a file is linted only if some config object's `files` matches, plus ESLint's always-linted default set (`.js` / `.cjs` / `.mjs`). Every rule-bearing object here is scoped to TS-and-TSX, and `.mts` / `.cts` are in **neither** the glob nor the default set. ⇒ The extension falls through both.

`priority:p3`, and the population is why: **one file, repo-wide** (no `.cts` files exist), counted with the same 4440-file walk #7908's gate uses. ⚠️ But it is not a trivial file — *"it defines every project, include glob and setup file the entire test run uses, and it is the one config in this repository that no lint run has ever read."*

⚠️ ⭐ **And it cannot be caught by objectui#7908's gate, by construction** — that gate reports files ESLint **walks**, and this file is not one of them. ⇒ Landing #7908 (graded `p2` today) does **not** close this, and ⛔ nobody should read that card's completion as covering `.mts`.

**Route: prefer option 2 — gate the gap.** Extend `check:lint-rule-coverage` with a second predicate over source extensions ESLint reaches for **neither** reason, so a `.mts` or `.cts` added later is **reported** rather than silently outside every run. ⇒ That scales with the repo and needs no red-set measurement to be safe. ⚠️ It is a real widening of that gate's subject and deserves saying so explicitly in the PR.

⚠️ **Option 1 (widen the glob) requires measuring the red set first**, and ⛔ must not be taken as "one line, obviously right": the same objection #7908's dispatch raised for the `.js` family applies — the red set is **unmeasured**, and turning rules on for a config file nothing has ever linted is a rule-**strength** decision, not a coverage fix. ⇒ If both are done, the gate lands first so the widening's red set is visible before it is chosen.

⛔ Correctly split from objectui#7908 rather than folded in: that card's dispatch scoped it to making **vacuity** visible and explicitly left rule-strength decisions out.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

Triage has argued the pull; the dev must still weigh it, and *"the predicate is not worth its maintenance"* is an admissible answer here if the measurement says so.

## ⭐ The dev found a third unreachable extension that neither the card nor triage names

The card scopes the defect to `.mts` / `.cts`. Re-derived here on a clean `origin/main` extract, every rule-bearing `files` entry in `eslint.config.js`:

```
**/*.{ts,tsx}      **/*.test.{ts,tsx}      **/__tests__/**/*.{ts,tsx}      **/*.tsx      packages/types/src/objectql.ts
```

⇒ `.jsx` is named by none of them, and ESLint's always-linted default set is `.js` / `.cjs` / `.mjs`. **`.jsx` is unreachable for exactly the same reason**, and nothing has ever reported it because the population is zero today (`.mts` 1, `.cts` 0, `.jsx` 0; control `.tsx` **2504**). ⭐ That is the finding restated one size larger: a listed special case would have shipped the blind spot at a smaller radius, which is why the dev derived the unreachable set from the live config on every run — one synthetic probe per source extension — instead of writing `.mts` into the gate.

## ⛔ Two premises re-derived, and both had moved

- **`4440` is stale — the walk returns 4480 today.** The dispatch required the number taken, not carried, and it was.
- **objectui#7908 has LANDED.** Verified on GitHub: closed 2026-09-07T14:04:29Z, and `scripts/check-lint-rule-coverage.mjs` is present on `origin/main`. ⇒ The dev wrote predicate 2 beside what is actually in the tree rather than beside the card's description of it, which is what the brief asked for and is why this is an extension of an existing gate rather than a new one.

The card's own three controls reproduce as **three distinct states**, not collapsed — `vitest.config.mts` ignored with `config: undefined`, `playwright.config.ts` at 116 rules, `scripts/github-slug.mjs` walked with 0 rules — corroborated from `lint:root`'s own `--format json` population of 275 files, with `vitest.config.mts` in none of them.

## ⭐ The ablation is five legs and each one answers a different objection

| leg | what it rules out |
|:--|:--|
| **A** — the gate at its base blob, hash-matched on disk | exit 0 with **zero** occurrences of `vitest.config.mts`: the defect really is invisible to the gate as it stands |
| **B** — inject `scripts/ablation-injected-tool.cts` | exit **1**, naming it |
| **C** — identical bytes, identical directory, `.ts` instead | exit 0, walked count 4480 → 4481 ⇒ **B's red is about the extension, not the file** |
| **D** — identical bytes as `.cts` inside `packages/core/dist/` | exit 0, not reported ⇒ the extension gap is separated from location exclusions |
| **E** — widen the two rule-bearing globs to reach `.mts` | exit **1 in both shrink-only directions** — `unreached-over-broad` naming the file, and `unreached-stale` printing `Delete the row` |

⭐ **Leg E is the one that matters most**, and it is the answer to the objection this seat would otherwise have raised: a ledger row is a waiver, and a waiver that survives its own remedy is a permanent exemption. It cannot survive — the moment the real fix lands, the gate demands the row's deletion. Each leg proved its mutation reached disk by **hash and marker count before any result was read**, ran under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths, and restored **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty), never by exit code.

⭐ And the ledger's rows are exact **paths**, not population globs, with the asymmetry against `VACUOUS_GROUPS` pinned by a test — because a `**/*.mts` row would waive the only thing the predicate exists to catch. That is the difference between a debt list and a hole.

## ⭐ Option 1 was measured and NOT taken, which is the behaviour the dispatch demanded

The dev measured triage's option 1 under trap-and-restore: with `mts,cts` added, `vitest.config.mts` resolves **116 rules** and `eslint vitest.config.mts` exits 0 **with no output — the red set is empty.** An empty red set is the most tempting possible moment to switch routes silently. It did not: option 1 stayed out of this PR and went to **#8469** with the number attached, on the reading that turning rules on for a never-linted population is still a strength decision with its own owner. ⇒ ⛔ Confirmed by this seat: that reading is correct, and the note that any widening must decide about **three** extensions rather than two belongs with it.

## The costs are stated rather than hidden

The four-axis answer concedes the fourth axis partly stands — the live population is one file, and `.cts`/`.jsx` value is prospective — and argues it is ~90 lines inside an existing gate, no new script, no new workflow, no new CI minutes, one walk feeding both predicates (`isPathIgnored` is 1.9s of the gate's ~2s, so walking twice would double it). ⛔ No transition window and no `**/*.mts` grace period, per 创业阶段不渐进. **The gate's own header now records that this PR widened its subject and why predicate 1 cannot see predicate 2's population by construction.** ⇒ That is a subject moved on purpose, which is what triage asked to be said out loud.

`+590/-33` across the gate and its pin (27 tests, 20 before). `lint:root` run verbatim from `package.json`, 275 files, 0 errors, 32 pre-existing warnings, none in the changed files. `check-changeset-presence` exit 0, none owed, run rather than guessed. `check-governed-queue-guard --test`: NOT GOVERNED. Both filed findings (#8469, #8471) carry the `finding` label **only**, unassigned — ⛔ no half-state to repair.

⚠️ **#8471 is a real conflict and the dev resolved it correctly**: this session's attribution instruction ends commit messages with a trailer naming a model, while the dispatch contract bans a model identifier in any pushed artifact. It acted on the **stricter** instruction and filed rather than choosing silently — which is the rule working. ⇒ ⛔ This seat does not answer it either; the durable fix is dispatch-contract text, and that is governed surface.
